significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would license the form-(iii) conclusion that an internal readiness threshold integrating "commitment and verification-completion signals" governs </think>, is systematically crossed later than answer stability warrants, and has a difficulty-dependent optimum; this is more constraining than merely finding a stop-token direction. It establishes both a behavioral phenomenon—late stopping and a hard-problem safety margin—and a causal mechanism whose threshold controls the accuracy–token trade-off, thereby predicting when shorter reasoning should be safe and when extra verification should remain. Verified false would distinguishably rule out a unified, miscalibrated-threshold explanation of excess reasoning, consequential because s1 (Muennighoff et al., 2025) relies on external budget forcing rather than knowledge that a model-internal readiness criterion is valid, although "true readiness" and the exact difficulty relation remain somewhat underspecified. Topic-substitution check: replacing this specific two-signal, late-threshold, difficulty-dependent account with the generic efficient-reasoning topic would not support this score; the added mechanistic relation is what puts it above the topic median.

reach.justification: The named handles are the "stop-readiness signal," "threshold correction," and resulting "calibrated efficiency knob," rather than merely an explanatory description. These are ex ante handles because readiness is read during an unfinished trace and can trigger </think> before otherwise-wasted tokens are generated, leaving an action window for inference-time gating. After per-model re-extraction, the asserted late-readiness and "difficulty-dependent optimal threshold" relations predict what calibration should recover, but transfer is limited to models with explicit thinking delimiters and the claim does not specify an architecture-invariant quantitative law; likely downstream users include researchers and practitioners controlling inference cost or deployment latency. Topic-substitution check: efficient reasoning alone supplies no readiness signal or stopping knob, so the score rests on these claim-specific transferable handles rather than on the importance of the assigned topic.
